meta.scope: Suriname batch 5 (final dig) — Power sector (EBS, SPCS/Afobaka), core social transfers (AOV, AKB), minimum wage, additional districts, and residual non-oil activity. Completes deep intermediate coverage.

candidates.title: Energiebedrijven Suriname (EBS) — national power utility
candidates.description: State-owned power utility with monopoly on distribution and retail. Operates transmission and distribution; depends heavily on generation from SPCS (Afobaka hydro + thermal) and other sources.
candidates.notes: Core power-system node. Coastal grid access is relatively high; interior connection rates are low. Hydro variability (Afobaka reservoir levels) creates recurring supply risk and load-shedding threats.

candidates.title: SPCS / Afobaka hydropower and thermal
candidates.description: Staatsolie subsidiary that operates the Afobaka hydropower plant and associated thermal capacity. Supplies the large majority of electricity to the EPAR (Paramaribo-area) network.
candidates.notes: Primary generation node. Continuously cited in power-security analysis; low reservoir levels periodically force reliance on expensive thermal and emergency rental capacity.

candidates.title: Algemene Ouderdomsvoorziening (AOV) — universal old-age benefit
candidates.publisher: Ministry of Social Affairs / AOV Fund
candidates.description: Non-contributory universal old-age benefit for persons 60+. Largest social-transfer programme by coverage.
candidates.notes: Core lived safety-net node. Coverage has grown steadily; continuously cited as the primary income support for older adults across all districts.

candidates.title: Algemene Kinderbijslag (AKB) — general child allowance
candidates.description: Non-contributory child allowance for children 0–18. Second major categorical cash-transfer programme.
candidates.notes: Core family-support node. Continuously cited alongside AOV as one of the two backbone unconditional transfers in the social-assistance system.

candidates.title: Minimum wage
candidates.description: Statutory national minimum hourly wage. Periodically adjusted; share of workers earning below the threshold is higher in the interior and among Maroon and Indigenous workers.
candidates.notes: Labour-floor node. Continuously cited in poverty and informality analysis; enforcement and coverage gaps are largest outside the formal coastal economy.

candidates.title: District Commewijne — eastern coastal
candidates.description: Eastern coastal district adjacent to Paramaribo. Significant peri-urban and agricultural population.
candidates.notes: Completes the greater Paramaribo coastal set alongside Wanica and Paramaribo itself.

candidates.title: District Marowijne — eastern border
candidates.description: Eastern border district with mixed coastal and interior characteristics; material Maroon population presence.
candidates.notes: Eastern border node. Completes the set of major districts beyond the capital core and the deep western/southern interior.

candidates.title: Labour informality
candidates.description: Share of employed persons in informal employment (without social-security coverage). Structural feature of the labour market.
candidates.notes: Lived labour structure. Roughly half of workers are classified as informal; informality is associated with higher probability of earnings below the minimum wage.

candidates.title: Forestry and timber
candidates.description: Forestry and timber production and export statistics. Non-mining primary sector linked to interior livelihoods and land-use debates.
candidates.notes: Interior primary-sector node. Continuously cited in diversification and land-rights analysis alongside gold and agriculture.

candidates.title: Port of Paramaribo / logistics
candidates.description: Main seaport and logistics hub. Critical for imports, gold/oil-related cargo, and the staging of offshore project equipment (e.g. GranMorgu subsea campaign).
candidates.notes: Trade and project-logistics node. Continuously cited as the physical gateway for both ordinary commerce and the large capital imports associated with offshore development.

proposed_edges.basis: EBS distribution depends heavily on generation supplied by SPCS (Afobaka and thermal).
AOV is the largest categorical social-transfer programme.
AKB is the second major categorical cash-transfer programme.
The minimum wage is the statutory floor for formal and monitored employment.
Informality is a partition of total employment.
Forestry activity is concentrated in and linked to interior livelihoods.
The main port is located in and serves the Paramaribo metropolitan economy.
